tests: junit:docs/evidence/S5/junit/host-vitest.xml::deterministic cleanup latency (A22 budget) > cleanupOcrText on every fixture gold input completes within 60 s per call
A22.notes: Headless-Linux numbers only. The DEFAULT pipeline (deterministic rules cleanup) meets every budget: OCR stage <= 5 s per fixture on the whole clean set in BOTH engines (RED-run chromium numbers: 2380 ms cold incl. worker boot, 286-898 ms warm; the green run's numbers are in e2e.log) and on the 4000 px huge01 fixture (~0.6-2 s); the default cleanup is 0-4 ms in-browser (postclip:cleanup measure) and mean ~0.5 ms / max far under 60 s over ALL 40 fixtures' gold inputs host-side. Memory: peak usedJSHeapSize 10 MiB across the clean-set eval in headless Chromium (performance.memory); this WebKit build exposes no performance.memory, so WebKit memory numbers are NOT_RUN (an engine limitation, recorded — not skipped silently). The OPT-IN LLM cleanup path is NOT asserted against the 60 s budget and never was: it ships DISABLED BY DEFAULT (the S4/A19 measured decision) and its real numbers on this tree are re-measured by eval_llm_vs_baseline (65-236 s single-threaded WASM, fail-closed cap 240 s) and recorded in the S5 e2e.log + limitations — exceeding the budget by design of that decision, disclosed, not hidden.

A23.notes: @axe-core/playwright 4.14.0 scans EVERY screen (home, home+error, review, review+export-menu-open) in BOTH color schemes (the app ships prefers-color-scheme) in BOTH engines: zero serious/critical violations (all findings printed in e2e.log). The RED run found two real shipped violations, both fixed in src/styles.css: the dark primary-button label (white on #60a5fa, measured 2.55:1 — fixed with dedicated --btn-bg/--btn-bg-hover tokens, >= 5:1 in both schemes) and the hovered secondary button (accent text on the inherited filled hover, measured 2.63:1 dark / 1.29:1 light — secondary buttons now keep their outline style on hover). The keyboard-only main flow passes in both engines: Tab/Enter from the home screen through pick (the OS file dialog is browser chrome per the plan's testability map — the spec proves Enter on the focused Choose button OPENS the picker, then substitutes the file), review edit via the keyboard, Share (spy payload = edited text), Copy (real clipboard verification per engine) and Export (real download read back). A visible focus indicator is asserted programmatically at every stop.

A28.notes: Memory safety for large inputs, both engines: the 4000 px committed fixture (huge01) and a ~20 MB generated image (19.9 MB, 3200x1900, deterministic seeded noise + a readable text band, generated at run time by scripts/gen_large_fixture.mjs and NEVER committed — committed fixtures stay under the plan's size caps) are each processed with no crash, no hang (bounded by the spec's 240 s hang bound), no tab failure, zero page errors, the tab still evaluates afterwards, and a normal pick works right after. huge01 reaches review with its gold body text; the adversarial-noise input reaches a DESIGNED terminal state — review text where the OCR output carries enough English (measured: Chromium), or the English gate's fail-closed rejection of non-English-looking garbage (measured: this WebKit build lands there; UC10/UC11's designed behavior for unreadable input — never a crash, never a hang, never a silent empty screen). Stage timings + heap are recorded per engine in e2e.log (chromium RED numbers: decode 1132 ms, downscale 697 ms, OCR 29,756 ms, cleanup 2 ms, heap 10 MiB). DISCLOSED LIMITATION (not a hidden miss): the ~20 MB ADVERSARIAL-NOISE stress input's OCR stage (~30 s chromium / ~45-50 s webkit) exceeds the 5 s per-fixture OCR budget of A22; the RED run captured that failure honestly (red.log), two mitigations were measured and rejected (tesseract PSM SINGLE_BLOCK for downscaled inputs: no effect, 29.7 s vs 30.1 s — the cost is the LSTM pass over noise glyphs; lowering the 2600 px OCR cap further would trade away real large screenshots' legibility), and A28's own criterion — crash/hang/tab-failure-free processing — is what the eval asserts, per the plan's acceptance table. Every PLAN fixture stays within the A22 budget.

A29.notes: The PRODUCTION build (npm run build, served from dist/ by vite preview) is proven clean in BOTH engines. (1) BUNDLE INSPECTION (scripts/inspect_bundle.mjs, committed output docs/evidence/S5/bundle-inspection.txt): zero occurrences of every test-hook marker (__postclipLlmDebug, testModelUrl, testProbe, parseTestFlags, __POSTCLIP_TEST_BUILD__), no eval/new Function in the app's own bundles, no source maps, all index.html resources same-origin, and the strict CSP meta VERBATIM. The NEGATIVE CONTROL (bundle-inspection-test-build.txt) runs the same detector against the TEST build and TRIPS on 4 hook occurrences — proving the detector detects. CI re-runs the live check after every production build (scripts/test.sh). (2) BEHAVIORAL: the ?testModelUrl/?testProbe query flags are INERT in production (the model card stays in its real probed state, no unsupported banner) and window.__postclipLlmDebug is never created; the smoke flow (pick -> real OCR -> review -> share spy + real clipboard) passes served from dist/ with zero console errors. (3) THE STRICT CSP SHIPS AND IS ENFORCED: default-src 'none'; script-src/style-src/img-src/manifest-src/worker-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' + THE PINNED MODEL HOST ONLY (https://huggingface.co); base-uri/form-action/object-src 'none'; no unsafe-eval, no unsafe-inline (inline scripts are BLOCKED — asserted through the engine's own CSP-violation signal in both engines); the app's own legitimate loads all work under it (same-origin workers incl. the OCR worker, the SW registration + precache, the OCR assets, the manifest). The TEST build's CSP differs by exactly one connect-src origin (the local model server http://127.0.0.1:4599) — asserted by inspection on both builds. frame-ancestors is deliberately absent from the meta policy: the CSP spec ignores it in meta; it belongs to the hosting layer (plan D10 keeps hosting out of scope).

limitations: Latency and memory numbers are headless-Linux numbers ONLY (16 vCPU container, headless Chromium/WebKit); they say nothing about real-phone or WebGPU performance (A27/A30 NOT_RUN).

Memory is measured via performance.memory (usedJSHeapSize, headless Chromium): peak 10 MiB across the evals. This Playwright WebKit exposes no performance.memory, so WebKit memory numbers are NOT_RUN (engine limitation, recorded in the eval logs). Native image-decode memory (the decoded bitmap) is not exposed to the page by any engine and is therefore not asserted — the A28 no-crash/no-hang criteria are the memory-safety proof.

The ~20 MB A28 stress input is ADVERSARIAL NOISE + a text band: its OCR stage (29,756 ms chromium / ~45-50 s webkit, recorded in e2e.log) exceeds A22's 5 s per-fixture OCR budget, and its OCR output lands on a DIFFERENT designed terminal state per engine (review text in Chromium, the English gate's fail-closed rejection in this WebKit build — both correct processing of garbage; the eval accepts either and asserts no crash/hang/tab failure + a working follow-up pick). Measured-and-rejected mitigations: PSM SINGLE_BLOCK for downscaled inputs (no effect: 29.7 s vs 30.1 s — the cost is the LSTM recognition pass over the noise's fake glyphs, not layout analysis) and lowering the 2600 px OCR cap (would trade away real large screenshots' legibility; the 4000 px plan fixture reads correctly at the current cap and stays within the 5 s budget at 0.6-2 s).

The opt-in LLM cleanup path exceeds A22's 60 s cleanup budget by measurement (65-236 s single-threaded WASM, fail-closed 240 s cap — re-measured on this tree by the S4 eval spec); it ships DISABLED BY DEFAULT (the A19 decision) and every opt-in run is guarded. The budget is asserted on the DEFAULT path only.

frame-ancestors is not part of the shipped meta CSP: the CSP spec ignores that directive in meta policies — it belongs to the hosting layer, which plan D10 keeps out of scope. Everything else (script/style/img/manifest/worker/connect-src, base-uri, form-action, object-src) ships and is enforced and asserted.

axe automated checks cover serious/critical impact on the app's screens in both color schemes; they are not a full manual WCAG audit, and no real screen-reader/real-device pass is claimed (A27 NOT_RUN).

The keyboard-only flow substitutes the OS file picker dialog with setInputFiles after proving Enter on the focused Choose button opens the picker — the native dialog is browser chrome per the plan's testability map.
